New Vision reports that the EMIS platform was redeveloped and rolled out in July 2022 to replace the Annual School Census, tracking learners and teachers online and verifying students across all levels of education, with registration mandatory for all schools.

New Vision reports that EMIS is a centralised platform developed by government and that under the June 2026 guidelines the Ministry of Education and Sports is primary custodian of all information entered into it.

The Ministry of Education and Sports launched new EMIS guidelines on 8 June 2026 at the National ICT Innovation Hub in Nakawa, with stricter compliance requirements and sanctions for officials and institutions that fail their data obligations, New Vision reports.

fact: The World Bank's ID4D diagnostic states that the Ministry of Education and Sports plans to use national identification numbers as the primary identifiers of pupils and students and so establish a functional register of learners, linked to EMIS, to track transfers, drop-out and fresh enrolment and to weed out ghost learners; the plan is undated, so the publication date is used.

An Auditor General's report quoted by The Kampala Report finds that critical administration and configuration of EMIS remain largely under the vendor, SMSOne, which has run them for four years under the ICT Ministry's supervision, with limited involvement of Ministry of Education technical staff; the report is undated, so the article's date of 9 June 2026 is used.
The EMIS launched in 2022 holds data on more than 13 million learners and staff from nursery to secondary level, according to The Kampala Report; the figure is undated, so the article's date is used.

The system holds individual learners' details, and those of all Senior One and Senior Five students are not yet fully captured because EMIS is not integrated with the UNEB system that should carry learner data from one level to the next; the article describes no entry of attendance or results and does not say who keys the records.
The Ministry of Education's Assistant Commissioner for Statistics says the contractor is upgrading the platform from EMIS 1.0 to EMIS 2.0 under a continuing contract, as reported on 9 June 2026.
The article gives no count or share of schools entering data; the system has been in service since 2022 and is described only by the 13 million learners and staff it holds.

The Ministry of Education and Sports states that it redeveloped the EMIS from 2019 under a memorandum with the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance, that MoES administrators run it, and that the old system had failed through donor dependence and abandonment by its software supplier.
The ministry's abstract reports pre-primary, primary and secondary schools responding to EMIS for the 2025 academic year: 7,408 pre-primary, 26,597 primary and 4,571 secondary.

The redeveloped EMIS collects individual learner-level data, issues a Learner Identification Number and tracks learner transfers, with heads of institutions as users; as of December 2025 the ministry counts 11,787,396 primary learners registered on it. The passages describe enrolment and transfer records and a 'data upload exercise', not attendance or results.

The Ministry of Education and Sports reports that 26,597 primary schools responded to the EMIS data upload for 2025, of 45,164 primary schools in the country (58.9%): 12,511 of 12,544 government schools and 14,086 of 32,620 private schools. The count is of schools that uploaded data, not of schools merely registered.

The ministry published its first annual statistical abstract since 2017, compiled from the redeveloped EMIS for the 2025 academic year; none could be produced for 2018 to 2024 after the annual school census was halted. No event date is given, so the publication date of January 2026 is used.

The Independent reports that the Ministry of Education runs EMIS, with its Assistant Commissioner for Statistics as EMIS focal person and ministry EMIS support staff stationed in every local government.

Schools register their learners on EMIS one by one: registered private schools had uploaded information for 2.3 million learners, and a headteacher says some directors tell heads to register only five learners where a school has 300. No entry of attendance or results is described; no date is given for the figures, so the article's date is used.

Of 61,572 private schools, 31,464 (the article says approximately 50 per cent) had registered on EMIS, as The Independent reports from a ministry briefing; the count is of private schools of all levels merely registered, not of primary schools entering data, and the article adds that those registered fall well short in the data they submit. No date is given for the figures, so the article's date is used.
